A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with Re-CatVTON renamed DeCo-VTON. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support matching content across the extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original VITON-HD and DressCode evaluations, component ablations, guidance-scale experiments, reference-network visualizations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds high-resolution evaluations, a leave-one-out loss ablation, and a blind human-preference study.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains full UNet fine-tuning, garment-free unconditional inputs, person-only DREAM supervision, and forward-diffused garment-latent replacement. Improved CFG, outfit-only loss, and GT Injection become Garment-Free Guidance, Decoupled Loss, and Clean Latent Anchoring. v2's fixed-noise and inference-only explanations add documentation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: VITON-HD and DressCode remain the training and evaluation datasets with the same garment categories. v2 Figure 1 adds in-the-wild qualitative try-on examples beyond v1's benchmark examples. The added high-resolution experiments retain the existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Reported comparisons expand substantially: PromptDresser joins Table 1; Voost and Voost (VTON-only) appear in Tables 6–7; RefTON and RefTON+R appear in Tables 8–9. RefTON also joins the appendix qualitative comparisons. These introduce transformer-based comparison families beyond v1's comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation at 1024x768 alongside the retained 512x384 experiments. It introduces a randomized blind A/B preference protocol with an Equal option, 25 participants, 30 samples, and 1,500 responses across two comparisons. The progressive ablation also replaces v1's reproduced CatVTON control with an explicitly identified, source-reported full-fine-tuning control; this does not establish that the earlier experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a focused leave-one-out test removing only Decoupled Loss at both resolutions, addressing dependence on progressive ablation ordering. The progressive ablation's baseline comparison is revised. Existing guidance-scale sensitivity and DressCode category analyses remain, with the guidance plot moved into the main text.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A.5 adds binomial and chi-squared significance testing for the user study, reporting p<0.001 for both comparisons. This statistical addition is confined to the new study. The existing 30-run latency averaging remains unchanged, and neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals or training-seed variability.

E6.justification: The proposed model's original benchmark and efficiency scores remain unchanged. v2 adds high-resolution results, including paired FID 4.741 on VITON-HD and 2.216 on DressCode, new comparator scores, and leave-one-out results. Figure 7 reports preferences of 62.0% versus 18.5% against CatVTON and 53.6% versus 25.9% against Leffa, with remaining responses ties. CatVTON's Table 1 paired FID/KID/LPIPS changes from 5.888/0.513/0.061 to 5.425/0.411/0.057. These additions and revisions do not represent same-setting improvements between versions of the proposed model.

T1.justification: The input, guidance, and DREAM-loss equations remain mathematically equivalent across notation changes. v2 explicitly writes standard diffusion and loss formulas for procedures already described in v1. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs; the revised conflict-based reasoning is conceptual interpretation.

C1.justification: v1 presents three conditioning hypotheses and an efficient CatVTON improvement. v2 centers the contribution on explaining full-fine-tuning failure through three conflicts and claims the first effective resolution under spatial concatenation. Its abstract and conclusion add first-visualization-study, broader single-network state-of-the-art, and human-preference claims, substantially redefining the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v2 strengthens the earlier hypotheses into explanations involving garment leakage, competing reconstruction gradients, and train-test discrepancy. It interprets the retained guidance experiment as diagnosing these conflicts and adds a resolution-dependent interpretation of the loss ablation. Limitations shift from garment-body correspondence and pose conditioning toward validation only on UNet/CFG models, possible DiT and flow-matching adaptations, and broader inpainting applications.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents reuse of a fixed noise sample for anchoring and clarifies that anchoring changes inference only. It removes v1's explicit 80GB memory-fit guidance, per-GPU batch explanation, and pixel-versus-latent implementation discussion. The actual latent concatenation, principal hyperparameters, hardware, software versions, and efficiency-measurement instructions remain documented.

R1.justification: Positioning expands from the single-versus-dual UNet efficiency gap to conditioning conflicts across architectures. Voost motivates the full-fine-tuning argument, while RefTON provides a distinct sequence-conditioning comparison. Added discussion connects the work to multimodal transformers, ControlNet, BrushNet, RePaint, and SDEdit, including explicit acknowledgment of prior known-signal anchoring approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conditioning analysis, method explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around a question–conflict–principle narrative. The model and components are renamed, related-work subsections are consolidated, experimental sections are reorganized, and supplementary material is redistributed into Appendices A–D.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout. v2 removes the structural-comparison schematic and logo close-up panel, revises the architecture diagram, merges the main qualitative comparisons and efficiency tables, and moves the guidance plot into the main text. It adds a user-study chart and comparison/ablation tables, while appendix image grids gain RefTON columns.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through higher-resolution and transformer comparisons, direct human-preference evidence, and a leave-one-out control beyond v1's progressive ablation. These make practical quality and component contributions easier to assess. The gain is tempered by stronger causal and architecture-independent claims: the recipe is not tested on a DiT backbone, and Table 10 shows small low-resolution loss benefits with worse paired KID. Overall, the evidence improves more clearly than the support for the broader mechanistic claims.
